comparator.name: Econometrics and Operations Research
comparator.academicYear: 2026–2027; current annual guide and adopted regulations, checked 2026-10-26
comparator.sourceNotes: The selected 2026–2027 pathway totals 180 EC: ten 6 EC compulsory units in Year 1; ten 6 EC Year-2 units, retaining all three part-II subjects; and 30 EC open study, three 6 EC restricted electives and a 12 EC thesis in Year 3. The selected electives are Econometrics III, Mathematical Economics III and Financial Econometrics; they are choices, not requirements for every student. The thesis follows the Econometrics specialisation. Open study remains subject to level, approval and entry conditions. Mandatory zero-credit study-support and English-language requirements sit outside the 180 EC. This is one valid pathway, not every possible combination. Year 1 is 60 EC. Its annual guide lists BRIDGE, SAM Programme EOR/EDS and the English Language Test at 0 EC; the narrative explicitly requires a full-year zero-credit course and the diagnostic. They are recorded separately, without interpreting their coexistence as extra credits. A failed English diagnostic requires the refresher; the introductory EOR grade requires the language condition. BSA normally requires 42 first-year EC and a pass in at least one calculus/analysis course AND at least one Probability Theory/Statistics course, subject to the regulations. Year 2 is 60 EC: seven compulsory units and the three prescribed part-II units retained here; one part-II may be replaced only with prior programme-director permission. Integrative Practical requires a partial mark of at least 5.5 in at least one of Econometrics I/Mathematical Economics I/Operations Research I. Advanced Practical requires a pass from each group: Statistics/Probability Theory(EOR)/Introduction to Data Science(EDS); Programming/Numerical Methods; and Econometrics I/Mathematical Economics I/Operations Research I. Thesis entry requires 120 EC including the relevant part-II course; Econometrics II is retained for this Econometrics thesis. The thesis is independent academic research with a paper and uploaded/presented poster, supervisor and second-reader assessment; register for Canvas and use Onstage. Submission before 1 July and approval before 1 August are needed for the stated pre-September graduation process, not extra EC. Tutorial/practical attendance may be required under individual manuals. Open Year-3 study is 30 EC: at most 6 EC at level 100, at least 12 EC at level 300, normally 90 EC for minor entry; prior board approval is required except stated faculty/university/Education-minor exemptions. The Economics university minor is unavailable to EOR students. Exchange, internships and individual packages need their applicable permissions. Honours and transitional arrangements are not stacked into this pathway. Material source reconciliation: the guide elective narrative says choose one or two of nine broader electives; the adopted OER Appendix VII annual chart says at most two. The selected Financial Econometrics plus two Ect/OR/ME-III subjects satisfies both, without relying on the disputed zero-other-elective interpretation. Financial Econometrics follows Econometrics III in P5; the other two are P4. This retains the neutral Econometrics route and a breadth subject from mathematical economics, adding the degree’s evidenced financial application; the choice is unrelated to UCR fit. The annual chart visibly calls E_EOR3_TR3 Econometrics II, but its code and the current guide/Pure course establish Econometrics III. Visible year and version 26-2-2026 agree; no older hidden edition was used.

routeSelection.basis: The normalized target is the generic Econometrics and Operations Research bachelor, whose current official curriculum lets students choose one of three third-year specialisations: Econometrics, Operations Research or Mathematical Economics. Econometrics and Operations Research are equally central to the programme's identity (both name the degree and both run through a compulsory I-II sequence), and neither is less specialised than the other, so no route is clearly more representative. Econometrics is selected by the neutral tie-break as the first specialisation in the order the official curriculum prints them. The choice was fixed before any UCR course selection and does not depend on UCR fit. The current 2026–2027 thesis entry explicitly refers to the chosen graduation specialisation; the recruitment page names Econometrics first. The three Year-3 electives are instantiated choices under that route, not three simultaneous specialisations.

core: Mathematical analysis, calculus and mathematical reasoning
Probability theory, statistics and statistical inference
Programming, data handling and computational quantitative analysis
Econometrics: regression, estimation, forecasting and multivariate time-series analysis
Operations research: mathematical optimisation, algorithms and decision-making under uncertainty
Mathematical economics: formal models of individual, strategic and market behaviour
Macroeconomics and finance as application foundations
Applying quantitative methods to integrated cases, quantitative research and presenting results to non-specialists
adjacent: Operations Research specialisation and the planning of capacity and service systems
Quantitative analysis of energy systems and sustainable production
questions: How do economic and financial shocks propagate, and what are their short- and long-run effects on inflation, employment and output?
How can scarce hospital capacity such as beds and doctors be planned and used efficiently?
How can production be optimised for lower material and energy use, and how does variability in solar and wind generation affect energy output and electricity prices?

trace: teaches structured and object-oriented programming in Python together with elements of discrete mathematics and computational problem solving, the programming foundation for all later computational work
covers differentiation, integration techniques, complex numbers and differential equations, the calculus foundation that the later modelling courses assume
develops logic, discrete structures and the mathematics of decision-making with applications to algorithm construction, supplying formal reasoning and the discrete foundations of optimisation
treats systems of linear equations, matrices, vector spaces, eigenvalues and Markov chains, the matrix methods used throughout estimation and optimisation
provides a foundation in mathematical statistics: probability theory, discrete and continuous distributions, sampling, parameter estimation and simulation
introduces research design and descriptive and inferential statistics up to analysis of variance, applied in a group research project
develops data cleaning, manipulation and visualisation skills and ends with an independent data-analysis project answering a research question
introduces relational database theory, SQL and query processing, the data-management layer on which large empirical and planning datasets are handled
treats numerical root finding, interpolation, differentiation, integration and differential equations, with explicit attention to algorithmic accuracy and sensitivity to input

Studies linear time-invariant signals, convolution and Fourier/Laplace/Z transforms. It contributes mathematical systems analysis; no state-space, stochastic time-series or financial-shock estimation equivalence is claimed.
teaches the design and experimental performance analysis of algorithms and data structures, on which efficient optimisation procedures depend
studies advanced algorithmic techniques and solution methods for optimisation problems, with emphasis on algorithmic thinking and mathematical modelling
covers search, constraint satisfaction, convex optimisation and linear and non-linear programming, with laboratory projects implementing them
treats planning and optimal behaviour under uncertainty, partial observability and resource constraints in deterministic and non-deterministic environments
Develops multivariate regression, factor analysis, analysis of covariance, logistic regression and reporting for human-science research; not specialist econometric time-series estimation.
introduces regression, classification, resampling and shrinkage methods for prediction, the statistical-learning side of forecasting

teaches OLS, GLS and instrumental-variables estimation, t, F and LM tests and Monte Carlo study of sampling distributions, and requires an empirical paper estimating economic relationships and making predictions
introduces supply and demand, game theory, consumer and firm theory, market structure and the macroeconomics of output, unemployment, inflation and financial markets
analyses national income, growth, inflation, unemployment, business cycles, economic crises and the effects of fiscal and monetary policy
develops advanced microeconomic theory: decision-making under uncertainty, imperfect competition and strategic behaviour, general equilibrium, market efficiency and externalities
Examines biases, heuristics, framing and experiments in economic decision-making; behavioral economic inquiry rather than a formal mathematical-economics sequence.

Develops accounting theory and financial-statement/annual-report analysis. This is business-information context, not evidence of asset pricing, portfolio theory or capital budgeting despite the course title.
examines fairness and bias, privacy, responsibility and accountability in automated and algorithmic decision systems
Introduces sustainability through planetary boundaries and environmental thresholds; prepares later sustainability study, without establishing technical energy-system design by itself.
extends the sustainability foundation through waves, chemistry and materials science and is the formal gateway to renewable-system design
covers the drivers and impacts of anthropogenic climate change and societal responses including renewable energy systems, the problem that energy-transition analysis addresses
evaluates the environmental impact of products and processes across their whole life cycle and circular-economy strategies, the analytical frame for reducing material and energy use in production
assesses energy-usage patterns and solar, wind and bioenergy options through combined technical and economic analysis, reported to a partner company
carries out team research on a sustainability problem supplied by a regional company or institution, applying the programme's methods to a real external case

analyses market failure, public goods, externalities and taxation with theoretical models and empirical evidence, the welfare framework in which interventions in energy markets and emissions are evaluated
examines the main moral theories and applies them to practical questions including climate change and obligations to future generations

alternatives.label: Quantitative economics and computational optimisation
alternatives.labelReason: The actual courses build mathematical/statistical and programming foundations, applied econometric estimation, AI optimisation and economic analysis. The label avoids promising a dedicated mathematical-economics or finance sequence.
alternatives.concept: Builds mathematical and statistical foundations for quantitative economic inquiry through programming, numerical methods, algorithms, AI optimisation, regression-based econometrics and economic theory. This is a substantive but qualified response to the EOR degree: one econometrics course and computational optimisation do not reproduce its advanced econometric, stochastic-OR, finance and mathematical-economics sequences or thesis.
progression: Actual enriched-workbook prerequisites and assigned terms checked for all 24 placements. Mathematical Methods precedes Linear Algebra, Probability & Statistics, Numerical Methods and Linear Systems; programming precedes AI and algorithms. Introductory research/statistics and mathematical probability precede multivariate Statistics & Experimental Methods and Machine Learning, followed by Econometrics. Economics precedes advanced economic topics. In the energy option Sustainability I precedes Sustainability II, which precedes Renewable System Design; the applied delta project follows research and domain foundations. Four courses per term, 180 EC, 24 unique courses, seven level-300 courses and Year-1 PPD all pass. Linear Systems remains a signals-mathematics complement, not state-space econometric estimation.

alternatives.label: Quantitative methods, sustainability and energy
alternatives.labelReason: Eight substitutions (60 EC) shift the application domain to sustainability, material life cycles, climate, public economics and renewable-system design, while retaining mathematical, statistical and optimisation methods. No specialist energy-price econometrics is promised.
alternatives.concept: Combines mathematical/statistical and computational methods with climate, life-cycle analysis, public economics, renewable-system design and an external sustainability project. It responds to the evidenced sustainable-production and energy questions through technical/economic analysis and general estimation tools; no selected course guarantees energy-market time-series modelling or stochastic electricity-price forecasting.

alternatives.distinctness: The closest match treats macroeconomics, finance, behavioural economics and algorithm design as the application and methods context of econometrics and operations research. This alternative instead organises the same quantitative core around the programme's evidenced energy and sustainable-production questions. That choice removes eight courses of the closest match — Logic & Discrete Mathematics, Database Management Systems, Algorithms & Data Structures, Advanced Algorithms, Accounting & Corporate Finance, International Macroeconomics, Behavioral Economics and AI Ethics — and adds eight that the energy concept requires: Sustainability Essentials I and II, Climate Change, Life Cycle Analysis & Circular Economy, Renewable System Design, Research in a Sustainable Delta, Public Economics and Ethics. The two programmes therefore share sixteen of twenty-four courses and each contains 60 EC the other lacks, and the difference is a change of application domain and of the economics taught (public economics of externalities rather than macroeconomics and finance), not a reshuffle.
traceOverrides: Provides AI planning under uncertainty and resource constraints; a possible method for energy-related decision problems, without a dedicated stochastic energy-market model.

Provides OLS/GLS/IV estimation, tests and an empirical paper. These general tools can inform economic energy questions; the actual course does not guarantee energy-price time-series or volatility models.

selection.assessment: All 36 linked rows were checked against current official evidence. Twelve are generator-eligible: the primary owns six core quantitative/economic/programming/econometrics and shock-analysis interests (4326,4327,4330,4332–4334), with limited specialist-finance coverage stated. The two energy/production interests (4329,4331) generate the second composition with eight substantive substitutions, 60 EC exclusive on each side. OR/capacity planning (4328,4335) cannot justify a distinct third programme: existing algorithms, AI optimisation/planning and numerical methods already supply its available UCR response, without dedicated hospital planning or stochastic-OR depth. Mathematical Economics (4336) fails specialist feasibility: UCR does contain game-theory and general-equilibrium topics in economics, but lacks the dedicated mathematical-economics progression, network games and empirical-network methods. Networks (4337) similarly cannot be supplied by computer-network or graph-search courses. Rows 4338–4348 support curricular assessment; 4349–4351 are examples and 4352–4361 are career/further-study outcomes, not independent programme generators. The current homepage replaces the historical Brexit/interbank-loan example with bank impacts of an interest-rate shock; no continuing specific Brexit or interbank-loan teaching is promised. Current future pages substantiate the broader professions/applications. Stop at two evidence-backed, coherent and distinct alternatives; do not expand the list to three.

blocks: Both are the programme's opening calculus course: differentiation, integration and differential equations used as the basis for all later modelling. VU's course goes further into analysis.
Both are the dedicated linear-algebra course: systems of equations, matrices, vector spaces and eigenvalues.
Both are the dedicated numerical-methods course: numerical root finding, differentiation, integration and the accuracy of algorithms.

Analysis II and Mathematical Reasoning continues rigorous analysis and proof. UCR's Advanced Calculus is not scheduled in either alternative and Logic & Discrete Mathematics treats logic and discrete structures rather than analysis, so the component is left unmatched.
Both are the mathematical-probability course: probability theory and discrete and continuous distributions. UCR's course also covers estimation and simulation.

Both are the first-year statistics course covering descriptive and inferential statistics and hypothesis testing. UCR's course is applied and paired with research design; VU's is a mathematical statistics course, so the correspondence is in subject and function rather than in mathematical depth.

Both include linear-regression estimation, inference and prediction. VU develops matrix formulation, finite-sample and asymptotic theory and maximum likelihood; UCR includes OLS, GLS, IV and an empirical paper. This is a bounded introductory subject relationship, not equivalence to the full sequence.

Academic Skills: Probability and Inference integrates first-year probability and statistics in an empirical application with conditional expectation, the law of large numbers and the central limit theorem. UCR has no counterpart integrating these specific foundations.

Econometrics II continues the econometric sequence beyond introductory regression. UCR offers only one econometrics course, which is already matched to Econometrics I, so this component is left unmatched.

Econometrics III covers panel data models, vector autoregressions, impulse responses and cointegration. UCR teaches no panel-data or multivariate time-series econometrics; Linear Systems treats impulse responses mathematically but not as econometric estimation, so no counterpart is claimed.
Financial Econometrics develops nonlinear, time-varying and latent-variable models for financial risk and volatility. No selected UCR course establishes this specialist coverage.
Both are the introductory programming course in which students learn to write and debug programs for quantitative problem solving.

Both are the first optimisation course of the programme, covering linear and non-linear programming. UCR's course frames optimisation within artificial-intelligence search and constraint satisfaction.

The introduction to Econometrics, Operations Research and Mathematical Economics surveys the three fields of the degree, including network optimisation and complexity. UCR has no course introducing these three fields together.

Operations Research II teaches two-/multi-stage stochastic optimisation, dynamic programming, Markov decision processes, value/policy iteration and Q-learning. The selected AI-planning profile establishes related uncertainty and resource planning but does not establish those defining methods, so no counterpart is claimed.
Both are the macroeconomics course: output, inflation, unemployment, business cycles and fiscal and monetary policy.

Both address choices under uncertainty, strategic behavior and welfare/market efficiency. VU explicitly develops mathematical properties and calculations of decision models, including group choices and game theory. UCR provides related microeconomic theory, with no claim to equal formal breadth.

Mathematical Economics II continues the formal economic-theory sequence. UCR's only advanced microeconomic-theory course is already matched to Mathematical Economics I, and Behavioral Economics and Public Economics are applied rather than mathematical-economics courses, so no counterpart is claimed.
Mathematical Economics III is an advanced specialisation course in formal economic theory. UCR has no counterpart at this level.

Finance I covers investment decisions, asset pricing, portfolios and cost of capital. The selected Accounting & Corporate Finance profile establishes accounting and financial statements only, so no counterpart is claimed.

Both are the programme's ethics course addressing the responsible use of quantitative decision methods. AI Ethics concentrates on fairness, bias, accountability and privacy in algorithmic decision systems.
The Integrative Practical applies the programme's methods to business cases in small groups. No UCR course applies econometric and operations-research methods to integrated business cases.

The Advanced Practical continues case-based group work with reporting and presentation of quantitative solutions. Research in a Sustainable Delta is also a team project for an external partner, but it applies sustainability research rather than econometric and operations-research methods, so it is not claimed as a counterpart.
The minor is 30 EC of open profiling space with no fixed content. It is preserved as open space and not matched to any UCR course.
The bachelor thesis is an independent quantitative research project in the chosen specialisation. No scheduled UCR course is a thesis; UCR's optional independent research is shown in this row.

notes.text: UCR supplies substantial mathematical, statistical, programming, optimisation and economic study, but one econometrics course does not reproduce VU’s econometric sequence, financial-risk models, stochastic operations research, mathematical economics, integrated EOR practicals or 12-EC thesis. Accounting supports financial-statement analysis; Linear Systems treats signals. Neither establishes the missing finance or econometric time-series training. The energy option adds technical/economic and sustainability study, without guaranteeing energy-price forecasting. No course equivalence or automatic postgraduate eligibility is implied.

audience.programmeDescription: VU Econometrics and Operations Research develops mathematical and statistical models for economic and business decisions. Its common foundations lead into econometrics, operations research and mathematical economics, with open study, selected advanced subjects and an independent thesis. This comparison instantiates the Econometrics specialisation.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR can support two qualified approaches: quantitative economics with computational optimisation, and a distinct combination of quantitative methods, sustainability and energy. Their mathematics, statistics, programming, estimation and economic reasoning respond to central EOR questions. They offer less disciplinary depth: the selected courses do not reproduce advanced econometric time series and financial-risk models, stochastic operations research, mathematical-economics networks, integrated EOR practicals or the thesis. Accounting and signals analysis remain specific complements. These compositions do not establish course equivalence or automatic master’s eligibility.
